title.narrative: Provision of emergency life-saving support through Unconditional Cash transfer and Livestock inputs to 2700 drought affected vulnerable households in Baidoa Rural.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed six-month emergency livelihood support project under the Reserve Allocation Strategy aims to provide life-saving emergency livelihood and food security support to drought-affected and displaced households in Baidoa District, one of the epicentres of acute food insecurity and livelihood collapse in southern Somalia. lt/pgtltpgtIn line with the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Strategic Plan and the FSC cluster strategic objectives, the intervention responds to the compounded impacts of prolonged drought, displacement, market shocks, and weakened coping capacities among vulnerable populations, the five (5) priority districts in southern Somalia—Afgooye, Baydhaba (Rural), Tayeeglow, Xudur, and Buur Hakaba with ADRO interventions intended to be implemented in rural Baydhoba District, where communities are experiencing the highest severity of food insecurity and livelihood loss. The project will target 1,700 vulnerable households across 5 villages ltspangtLowiile (410HHs), Bula sagar (320HHs), Ashagow (400HHs), Lanbuli (270HHs) Adeyki (300HHs) lt/spangtltspangtthrough the provision of lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) combined with emergency livestock inputs (Cash+ approach).lt/spangtltspangt The intervention aims to ensure immediate access to food, sustain livestock health and productivity, and prevent further depletion of livelihood assets caused by prolonged drought and displacement.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtIn line with Food Security Cluster (FSC) guidance, targeted households will receive USD 55 per household per month, covering approximately 70% of the food Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), for a minimum of three (3) consecutive rounds. Cash assistance will be delivered through Hormuud EVC Plus as it is widely used in the target areas, ensuring safe, timely and accessible transfers. Complementing UCT, households will receive emergency livestock inputs focused on drought-responsive interventions, including animal water support/water trucking (7,000 livestock and 1,000 HHs), veterinary treatment and deworming, to stabilize 7,000 livestock conditions in 5 villages, reduce mortality, and support early recovery. These interventions are strictly focused on mitigating drought impacts, reducing livestock mortality, preventing disease outbreaks, and stabilizing household food and income sources. ltbrgtBeneficiary targeting will be conducted through inclusive community engagement, prioritizing the most vulnerable households, including female-headed households, IDPs, households with elderly persons, and persons with disabilities. Community Selection Committees (CSCs), in coordination with local authorities, will be trained on transparent and inclusive selection processes, with verification conducted through field visits, sampling, and key informant interviews.lt/pgtltpgtADRO maintains continuous access to all targeted villages and actively participates in ABC forums, FSC coordination meetings, and inter-agency platforms, while implementing similar FSC-aligned livelihood interventions. The organization will coordinate closely with INGOs, NNGOs, line ministries, and local authorities to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication, and strengthen referrals to Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Protection services.ltbrgtProtection mainstreaming, inclusion of at-risk groups, and accountability to affected populations (AAP) will be integrated throughout implementation. A toll-free hotline (2455) will remain operational for feedback and complaints, while Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) will be conducted after each UCT round and at project completion to assess effectiveness, identify gaps, and inform adaptive programming.ltbrgtThis Cash+ emergency response will restore immediate food access, safeguard livestock-based livelihoods through provision of water, veterinary care and deworming, and enhance the resilience of drought-affected households in Baidoa District, reducing reliance on negative coping strategies and humanitarian assistance.lt/pgt
